item.title: The Unceasing Breath: Prayer for the Woman Who Has No Time to Pray
item.description: You’re sitting at your office desk, waiting for payday to pay a stack of unpaid bills, while your adult daughter stops by for some motherly advice, and your phone buzzes with a text from your mother that her oxygen levels are dipping and she needs you to come by after work. You feel less like the "virtuous woman" of Proverbs 31 and more like a human panini—pressed between the heavy weights of two generations, with the heat of a toxic workplace turned up to high.

item.title: The Middle Ground: Remembering God’s Faithfulness in Waiting Seasons
item.description: In the moment by moment living where we are no longer where we have been, but not yet certain of where we are going, we can build our faith brick by brick in believing in who God is by His Word, who He has been before in our lives, and how He continues to be those things today. God does not change (Malachai 3:6), and we can hold to hope in Him with confidence, trusting that He will continue to come through for us, even in the wind-swept days where we long and wait for fullness once again.

item.title: When Talking to God Feels Too Hard
item.description: Tell God how hard it feels to talk to Him. Tell Him what you’re afraid to say. Let Him meet you in your own way, not someone else’s formula. Allow Him to show you how you communicate best with Him. Jesus told us to keep on asking, keep on knocking, keep on seeking (see Matthew 7). God desires a relationship with you. He wants your questions, your fears, your hopes, your anger, your joy—all of you.

item.title: What Forty Days Taught Me About Prayer
item.description: I went on to complete the 40 days, which took me about 45 days. And it was during this time that God opened my eyes to prayer in new, transformative ways.

item.title: Enhancing your Prayer Life through Confession
item.description: Confession seems like a scary word to us. Maybe we’ve watched too many crime dramas where confession leads to conviction, which means a lack of freedom.

item.title: Prayer Prompts
item.description: The Holy Spirit fills in the gaps when our knowledge is incomplete, but in other places, the Bible gives specific prayer prompts.

item.title: When Prayer Becomes the First Thing, Not Another Thing
item.description: God never created us to just push through. We were never supposed to do everything in our own strength. God created us for something far greater than survival. He created us to live in dependence on Him, to impact His Kingdom, and to walk in His grace.

item.title: Praying Boldly and Expectantly on Our Knees
item.description: Many of us have been taught to pray with faith, but not always with intimacy. We pray carefully. Respectfully. Sometimes even cautiously. And while reverence is holy, restraint born from disappointment can quietly rob us of boldness. We stop asking God to draw near, not because we don’t want Him, but because we don’t want to be let down again.

item.title: Prepare Yourself for the King
item.description: This time, my prayer was different. I asked God to change me—my heart, my mind, my attitudes, whatever He wanted. That prayer was difficult because it required me to get myself out of the way.

item.title: Everyday Power of Prayer
item.description: By Shara Beuler-RekpaThe Everyday Power of Prayer | When Faith Is Tested in the Waiting I By Shara Beuler RepkaIt was our prayers for guidance that sent our road ministry back to the West. The Lord kept us in our home state of Texas for a bit, but now He’d impressed on us it was time to roll.
